entries.cause: The redirect URI (reply URL) in the request is not registered for the application.
entries.fix: In the app registration's Authentication page, add the exact redirect URI from the request: scheme, host, port, path, and trailing slash must all match.

entries.cause: The user is not assigned to the application, and the application requires assignment.
entries.fix: Assign the user, or a group they belong to, in Enterprise applications > the app > Users and groups, or turn off Assignment required.

entries.cause: No application with this client ID exists in the tenant the user signed in to.
entries.fix: Check the client ID and the tenant in the sign-in URL. A single-tenant app must be used through its own tenant; a multi-tenant app must be consented in the user's tenant.

entries.cause: Neither the user nor an administrator has consented to the permissions the application asks for.
entries.fix: Have an administrator grant consent for the application, or let the user consent if tenant policy allows it.

entries.cause: The user declined the consent prompt.
entries.fix: Have the user sign in again and accept, or have an administrator grant consent for all users.

entries.cause: The user's account comes from another tenant or identity provider and is not a guest in this tenant.
entries.fix: Invite the user as a guest, or for a multi-tenant app sign in through the common or organizations endpoint instead of this tenant's.

entries.cause: The user account does not exist in this directory.
entries.fix: Check the username for typos and that the user is signing in to the right tenant.

entries.cause: The username or password is wrong.
entries.fix: Have the user retry or reset the password. Repeated failures from an app or script point at stored credentials that are out of date.

entries.cause: The account is locked, after too many failed sign-ins or because sign-ins came from a known malicious IP address.
entries.fix: Wait for the lockout to end or have an administrator unlock the account, and review the failed attempts in the sign-in logs.

entries.cause: The user's password has expired.
entries.fix: Have the user change the password, then sign in again.

entries.cause: The user account is disabled.
entries.fix: An administrator must enable the account again (Users > the user > Account enabled).

entries.cause: A silent sign-in (prompt=none) found no signed-in user.
entries.fix: Expected when there is no session: the application should fall back to an interactive sign-in. If the user is signed in, the browser may be blocking third-party cookies.

entries.cause: Multi-factor authentication is required, and the user has not completed it for this sign-in.
entries.fix: Have the user complete MFA. An application that signs in silently must fall back to an interactive sign-in.

entries.cause: The user must register for multi-factor authentication before signing in.
entries.fix: Have the user complete MFA registration when prompted, or at the My Sign-Ins page.

entries.cause: A Conditional Access policy blocked the sign-in.
entries.fix: Open this sign-in in the Entra sign-in logs: its Conditional Access tab names the policy and the condition that failed.

entries.cause: Conditional Access requires a compliant or managed device, and this device is not one.
entries.fix: Bring the device into compliance (for example by enrolling it in Intune), or sign in from a managed device.

entries.cause: Entra ID stopped a sign-in loop: the same browser asked it to sign in too many times in a short period.
entries.fix: Find why the application does not accept the sign-in it receives and starts another one, often a cookie or session problem in the application.

entries.cause: The token request carries no client secret or client assertion, but the application is registered as a confidential client.
entries.fix: For a browser or mobile app, register its redirect URI under the Single-page application or Mobile and desktop platform. Otherwise, send the client's credentials.

entries.cause: The client secret in the token request is wrong.
entries.fix: Check that the application uses the secret's value, not its ID, and that the secret has not expired or been replaced.

entries.cause: The browser redeemed the code from another origin, which Entra ID allows only for redirect URIs registered as a single-page application.
entries.fix: Move the redirect URI to the Single-page application platform on the app registration's Authentication page.

entries.cause: The authorization code was already redeemed.
entries.fix: Redeem each code once. Look for a callback page that runs twice, for example after a reload.

entries.cause: The authorization code or refresh token has expired.
entries.fix: Redeem codes immediately after the callback. For an expired refresh token, sign the user in again.

entries.cause: The application asked for an ID token in the URL (the implicit flow), which is not enabled for it.
entries.fix: Switch to the authorization code flow with PKCE. If the implicit flow is truly needed, enable ID tokens under Implicit grant on the Authentication page.

entries.cause: The application asked for an access token in the URL (response_type=token), which is not enabled for it.
entries.fix: Switch to the authorization code flow with PKCE. If the implicit flow is truly needed, enable access tokens under Implicit grant on the Authentication page.

entries.cause: The application has no reply address registered.
entries.fix: Add the application's redirect URI, or for SAML its Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL), in the application's settings.

entries.cause: The redirect_uri value is not a valid absolute URI.
entries.fix: Send an absolute URI with a scheme and host, such as https://app.example.com/callback.

entries.cause: A required parameter is missing from the request.
entries.fix: The error_description names the missing parameter; make the application send it.

entries.cause: For the HTTP-Redirect binding, the SAMLRequest or SAMLResponse must be a query parameter in the URL, and it is not.
entries.fix: Send the AuthnRequest as a deflated, base64, URL-encoded SAMLRequest query parameter, or switch the SP to the HTTP-POST binding.

entries.cause: Entra ID could not read the SAML message.
entries.fix: Check that the SP sends a well-formed AuthnRequest with its binding's encoding: deflate plus base64 for HTTP-Redirect, base64 only for HTTP-POST.

entries.cause: The SP asked for an authentication method (RequestedAuthnContext) that differs from the one the user signed in with.
entries.fix: Remove RequestedAuthnContext from the SP's AuthnRequest, or have the SP accept the method the user signed in with.

entries.cause: AD FS stopped a sign-in loop: the same browser session made too many requests in a short time.
entries.fix: Find why the application sends the user back to AD FS instead of accepting the token, often a cookie, clock, or certificate problem at the application.

entries.cause: The request was signed with a different algorithm than the relying party trust expects, usually SHA-1 against SHA-256.
entries.fix: Make the relying party trust's secure hash algorithm match how the SP signs. SHA-256 is preferred.

entries.cause: AD FS has no relying party trust for the identifier the SP sent.
entries.fix: Make the SP's entity ID (the AuthnRequest Issuer) exactly match an identifier on the relying party trust.

entries.cause: The SP asked for an authentication method AD FS does not offer.
entries.fix: Remove or change RequestedAuthnContext in the SP's request, or enable that authentication method in AD FS.

entries.cause: Authentication failed: the credentials are wrong, or the user cannot sign in.
entries.fix: Check the username and password, and the user's status (locked, suspended, or deactivated) in the Okta admin console.

entries.cause: The caller does not have permission for the requested action.
entries.fix: Check the user's assignment to the app and the permissions of the token or client that made the call.

entries.cause: The token in the request is invalid.
entries.fix: Check that the token has not expired or been revoked, and that it was issued by this Okta org.

entries.cause: Okta's rate limit was exceeded.
entries.fix: Slow the client down and retry after the time given in the X-Rate-Limit-Reset response header.

entries.cause: The user's password has expired.
entries.fix: Have the user change the password, then sign in again.

entries.cause: The user account is locked.
entries.fix: Unlock the user in the Okta admin console, or wait for the lockout to end.

entries.message: User is not assigned to the client application.
entries.cause: The user is not assigned to this application in Okta.
entries.fix: Assign the user, or a group they belong to, to the app in the Okta admin console (Applications > the app > Assignments).

entries.cause: Google's SAML app does not match the request, usually because the SP's entity ID differs from the Entity ID set in the Google Workspace SAML app.
entries.fix: In the Google Admin console's SAML app settings, set the Entity ID to exactly the SP's entity ID (the AuthnRequest Issuer).

entries.cause: The SAML app is turned off for the user's organizational unit or group.
entries.fix: Turn the app on for the user's organizational unit or group in the app's User access settings in the Google Admin console.

entries.cause: The OAuth app is limited to users in its own Google Workspace organization, and this user is outside it.
entries.fix: Sign in with an account from that organization, or change the app's user type to External on its OAuth consent screen.

entries.cause: A Google Workspace administrator does not allow this user to grant access to the app.
entries.fix: Have the administrator trust the app in the Admin console's API controls.

entries.cause: Google refuses sign-in from embedded browsers (web views).
entries.fix: Sign in through the system browser, for example with the operating system's authentication session API instead of a web view.

entries.message: Cookie not found. Please make sure cookies are enabled in your browser.
entries.cause: Keycloak did not get its login session cookie back when the login form was submitted.
entries.fix: Allow cookies for the Keycloak host. In an iframe or another site's context, third-party cookie blocking is the usual cause; also check that proxy and hostname settings do not change the cookie's domain or path.

entries.cause: Keycloak did not get its login session cookie back when the login form was submitted: the cookie expired, was deleted, or the browser blocks it.
entries.fix: Start the sign-in again from the application. If it keeps happening, allow cookies for the Keycloak host; in an iframe or another site's context, third-party cookie blocking is the usual cause.

entries.cause: The username or password is wrong, or the user does not exist in this realm.
entries.fix: Have the user retry or reset the password, and check that the user exists in the realm the sign-in uses.

entries.message: Account is disabled, contact your administrator.
entries.cause: The user account is disabled in the realm.
entries.fix: An administrator must enable the user again (Users > the user > Enabled).

entries.cause: No client in the realm matches the request's client_id, or for SAML the AuthnRequest Issuer.
entries.fix: Check the client_id or SP entity ID, and the realm name in the URL, against the realm's Clients list.

entries.message: Your login attempt timed out. Login will start from the beginning.
entries.cause: The login page stayed open longer than the realm allows for a login.
entries.fix: Start the sign-in again. If users routinely need longer, raise the realm's login timeout.
